q: What do we know about feat-trv-funnel-v2 in the travel-spend-recovery project?
a: Search-to-book and quote-to-book conversion from the app booking funnel, built in April 2026. With it trv-ridge-v3 reaches 4.3% MAPE on trv-bt-2025h2, against 5.2% for trv-ridge-v2 on the same set (exp-505).

q: What came of exp-504 in the travel-spend-recovery project?
a: exp-504 tested a BSTS model with holiday effects: MAPE 5.6%, worse than the 5.2% ridge, and about three times the fit time. dec-trv-stop-bsts stopped the BSTS line.

q: What does trv-ridge-v3 use as inputs in the travel-spend-recovery project?
a: feat-trv-funnel-v2, feat-trv-cross-border-share and feat-trv-seasonality-adj. It does not use feat-trv-fx-vol, which was tested and excluded.

q: What is the current travel spend model in the travel-spend-recovery project?
a: trv-ridge-v3, adopted for the quarterly pack from June 2026. It supersedes trv-ridge-v2; the BSTS and STL models are not in use.

q: What share of its 2024 run-rate did cross-border travel spend reach by 2026-Q2 in the travel-spend-recovery project?
a: 101% of the 2024 run-rate, while domestic reached 96%. This overturned the earlier 88% plateau for total travel spend (fnd-trv-plateau).

q: Why does the travel-spend-recovery project now report domestic and cross-border travel spend separately?
a: The blended series hid a cross-border lag: total travel sat at 88% of the 2024 run-rate through 2025-Q3, and cross-border then recovered to 101% by 2026-Q2 while domestic was at 96%. dec-trv-report-split moved reporting to separate lines from June 2026.
